answer.rationale: Finance requires 18% unit-cost reduction; the contract expires in 14 days; the line runs at 94% with no buffer, so switching primary vendor or adding a second source mid-cycle raises delivery risk. Negotiation preserves the stable integration (per c1) while leveraging the proven playbook from c4 (benchmarking to move both price and payment terms) and the multi-year commitment leverage from c6 (volume pricing unlocked by longer terms, without narrowing service scope). Verifying c6 to confirm the term-length → unit-cost mechanism still holds under current market conditions before committing. Defer is rejected: finance mandate and contract cliff make delay more expensive than the option value of waiting.
